news.title: NZ Football pulls support for Infantino as FIFA President
news.lede: New Zealand Football has pulled its support for Gianni Infantino as FIFA President amid the fallout from the embattled executive's failed World Cup sell-off plan. NZ Football, which governs the game in Aotearoa, also called for an independent review of the steps taken during the plan's development. "After careful consideration, NZF has formed the view that decisions and actions within FIFA have contributed to a breakdown in trust and increased division within international football, and that an independent review is required to restore confidence and trust," it said in a statement. "NZF believes this point in time represents an opportunity for all FIFA member associations to advocate for stronger governance, accountability and transparency which are fundamental in maintaining confidence of the administration of the global game."

news.title: Soccer-FIFA crisis timeline: From World Cup final to global standoff
news.lede: Aug 14 (Reuters) – Here is a timeline of events where FIFA president Gianni Infantino introduced a proposal to sell a slice of the World Cup’s commercial future that backfired and sparked a global revolt in the sport:. July 19 – The first 48-team World Cup concludes at New York New Jersey stadium with Infantino and U.S. President Donald Trump, booed as they walked onto the pitch, presenting the trophy to Spain after their 1-0 win over Argentina. July 28 – Shortly after a leak in the British media, FIFA announces it wants to create a $20 billion subsidiary to run the World Cup and other competitions, raising $4.2 billion for soccer development by selling a 20% stake to external investors.

news.title: How the ASEAN Hyundai Cup™ Is Bringing Southeast Asia Together Through Football
news.lede: The ASEAN Hyundai Cup™, title-sponsored by Hyundai Motor, officially kicked off on July 24, marking the start of Southeast Asia’s biggest football celebration. As part of its growing global football portfolio alongside FIFA and CONMEBOL, Hyundai is connecting with millions of fans through the tournament, celebrating the passion, unity, and sense of belonging that sport inspires across communities. Now in its 30th year anniversary, the ASEAN Hyundai Cup™ remains Southeast Asia’s premier football tournament. Bringing together 11 ASEAN Member Associations, the competition opens with Cambodia hosting Singapore before continuing across the region in a home-and-away format.

news.title: ‘Breakdown in trust’: Fresh calls for Infantino to fall on sword as Kiwis take aim at FIFA
news.lede: New Zealand Football has joined the growing list of federations calling for sweeping changes at FIFA, withdrawing their support for embattled president Gianni Infantino. Infantino is facing the threat of civil war in the aftermath of his abandoned plan to sell off a 20 per cent stake in major FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup, to private equity. Called the FIFA Forward Enterprise, or FFE, the proposal united the football world in condemnation, with Infantino quickly aborting the scheme. news.title: Global Football Governance Crisis: Infantino's Controversial World Cup Proposal Unravels
news.lede: FIFA President Gianni Infantino's recent proposal to sell a 20% stake in the World Cup's commercial future has caused significant upheaval in the global football community. The plan, which sought to raise $4.2 billion for soccer development, bypassed the six regional confederations, sparking criticism over the lack of transparency and consultation. The controversial move drew ire from football bodies such as UEFA and CONCACAF, which criticized the absence of governance and transparency. Despite the initial pushback, Infantino eventually scrapped the plan on August 1, acknowledging the divisions it created within the football community.

news.title: ‘Full support’ for Infantino: Six Arab federations defy growing revolt over World Cup plan
news.lede: Six Arab football federations have thrown their weight behind Gianni Infantino, declaring their “full support” for the embattled FIFA president as opposition to his controversial World Cup investment plan continues to grow.The backing came from Morocco, Qatar, Egypt, Mauritania, Lebanon and Sudan on Thursday, with four of the six federation chiefs also serving on the FIFA Council. news.title: Referee Yiembe: From dusty fields of Nakuru, to Fifa Club World Cup and Uefa Super Cup
news.lede: Aston Villa's John McGinn remonstrates to assistant referee Stephen Yiembe during UEFA Super Cup final on Wednesday. Assistant referee Stephen Yiembe from Kenya boasts an impressive medal haul from officiating at major sporting championships across the globe. But Yembe’s story can’t be told without stating one caveat: Fifa does not allow referees to grant interviews to the media without clearance from the headquarters in Zurich. The latest addition to Yiembe’s medal collection is undoubtedly one of his most prestigious - the medal he received on Wednesday night after officiating the 2026 Uefa Super Cup final as one of two assistant referees.

news.title: New Zealand Football withdraws support for Infantino, urges review
news.lede: Gianni Infantino came under renewed fire this week after three confederations signed an open letter accusing the world football boss of breaking trust 'through deception'. (EPA Images pic) WELLINGTON: New Zealand Football said on Friday it had withdrawn support for Fifa boss Gianni Infantino and called for an independent review into his aborted plan to sell off part of the World Cup. Infantino came under renewed fire this week in an open letter signed by three confederations – Uefa, North and Central America's CONCACAF and Asia's AFC – accusing the world football boss of breaking trust "through deception". It is believed they want the Swiss official to resign before he has the chance to seek re-election in March next year.
